task.title: Reserve the next due schedule deterministically
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/841 by centralizing earliest-due selection and persisted race handling in the scheduler kernel.
acceptance_criteria: Select pending work by due instant then exact schedule ID through an explicit cutoff.
Return none when no eligible work exists and restart selection after persisted optimistic conflicts.
Fail closed on malformed history without ambient clock, dispatch, or execution authority.

attempts.diagnostic: Schedule-store tests failed because claim_next_due did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added focused integration coverage for the required success, absence or conflict, validation, and fail-closed paths.

attempts.summary: Implemented the bounded contract and refactored only demonstrated duplication.
attempts.diagnostic: The capability existed below the requested boundary or required one new typed kernel operation.
attempts.patch: Composed list_due ordering with exact-revision claim, retried persisted selection conflicts, and added ordering, persistence, concurrency, and corruption tests.

outcome.summary: Concurrent callers can reserve distinct earliest-due schedules while malformed durable evidence still blocks selection.

lessons: Centralize deterministic selection where ordering and optimistic concurrency can be enforced together.
Retry only a persisted selection race; do not broaden that mechanism into execution retry policy.
Repeated concurrent tests supplement, but do not replace, deterministic contract coverage.
